texts.content_exam: Summer camps are becoming more and more popular with young people, but what are they like? Last month, a school reporter called Sally Henshaw travelled to Loch Lomond, Scotland. 'I travelled for about ten hours.' Finally, it was dark when the minibus drove past a sign, I heard someone saying 'Welcome to Camp Lomond'. As soon as I heard that voice I just wanted to go indoors and jump into a nice, soft bed. However, the camp leaders had other ideas. We all had a barbecue, and then we sat around a campfire and talked. Finally, one of the leaders divided us into groups of three and said:'Now it's time to put up your tents', I don't know how three of us managed to sleep in a tent the size of a single bed, but somehow we did.

texts.content_exam: When we woke up the next day, my new friend Ingrid opened the front of the tent, and we all looked out. There was Loch Lomond. 'Loch' means 'lake' in Scottish, and Loch Lomond is one of the most beautiful places I've ever seen! That morning after breakfast, we went horse-riding around the lake. In the next few days, the camp organized different activities. Most sports activities are in the afternoon, and in the morning, you can choose lessons like drawing, chess, drama and cookery. I've never been very good at art and I'm not a great actress, so I went along to the cookery class. I love food. The best things about the camp were learning new things and making new friends. Finally, since I came home, Ingrid and I have been texting every day.

texts.source_text: Celebrations of Culture From Around the World
texts.content_exam: Getting people together is at the heart of what we love about planning parties and events around the world. There are many reasons to get family and friends in one place celebrate and carry on traditions that have been around for many generations. So, why don't we take a tour of some of the world's biggest gatherings? Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta: Hundreds of balloons set flight at this fiesta which lasts for 9 days in October in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Kids and adults alike gather to the massive launch site for its festival to see countless floating balloons of all shapes, sizes and colors light up the desert sky. Águeda, Portugal: Águeda's streets get a bright inspiration in July, as colorful umbrella canopies line the streets of this town.

💡 الشرح: النص يقول: 'Getting people together is at the heart of what we love about planning parties and events around the world.'

texts.source_text: Celebrations of Culture From Around the World (Continued)
texts.content_exam: From the 7th to the 29th of July, visitors and locals can expect art setting up, performances and many street arts as the festival Águeda takes place. Yi Peng Lantern Festival: The sky of Chiang Mai in Thailand is set shining as thousands of lanterns are released throughout the city during the Yi Peng Lantern Festival. This citywide gathering takes place on the evening of the full moon on the 12th month of the Thai lunar calendar (usually November) and is often celebrated alongside Loy Krathong during three days of parades, markets, candle lightings and more. Holi Festival of Color, India: It is a celebration of the triumph of good over evil and the arrival of spring. Holi is a colored-powder-throwing party well-known in different cultures.
